adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Tokens from `usernames.split(",")` are not stripped, so a caller sending "user1, user2" (space after comma, plausible from hand-built API calls) silently fails to find " user2" via `find_by_username` and that member is silently skipped with no error reported to the caller

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and passes each token directly to `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. If the incoming `usernames` param is a comma-separated string with spaces (e.g. "user1, user2"), the second token will be " user2" and will not match a normal username lookup, causing that user to be silently skipped (the code ignores non-matches and still returns success unless `group.save` fails). This is a concrete correctness issue introduced/visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — resources :groups` still routes PATCH /admin/groups/:id to the same `update` action (the old `request.patch?` branch to the safe `update_patch` was removed), and `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs unconditionally, so a stale/legacy client still issuing the old incremental `PATCH ... changes: {add/delete: ...}` payload (no `visible` key) will now silently force the group's `visible` flag to false and save instead of erroring or leaving it untouched

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Rails, `resources :groups` generates a `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` route to the `update` action by default. In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` no longer branches on `request.patch?` (the old `update_patch` path handling incremental membership changes was removed), and it now always executes `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. If a legacy client still sends the old incremental PATCH payload (`changes: { add/delete: ... }`) without a `visible` param, then `params[:visible]` is nil and the expression evaluates to `false`, causing the group’s `visible` flag to be silently set to false and saved. This behavior is directly verifiable from the updated controller code and standard REST routing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1 — {{#if model}}` still gates the members table on the group model itself, but `model` is now always a (truthy) Group object rather than the old bare members array, so a group with zero members now renders an empty table (header row only) instead of nothing as before; the guard was not updated to check `members`/`user_count` for the new response shape

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — create` reads only `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]`, never `params[:alias_level]`, even though the client's shared `Group#asJSON()` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:62-68) always sends `alias_level` in both create and update payloads, so an alias level chosen on the "new group" form is silently discarded on save (pre-existing gap, still present after the params-shape refactor touched these exact lines)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, the client’s `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` returns `{ name, alias_level, visible }` and `Group#create()` POSTs that payload to `/admin/groups`. However `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` (and never reads `params[:alias_level]`), while `update` *does* handle `params[:alias_level]`. So when creating a new group, any alias level chosen in the form is ignored and the group will be created with the model/default alias level instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10 — Pagination state (limit/offset/user_count) lives as raw model properties but is computed on in admin-group.js.es6 (currentPage/totalPages) and mutated directly by next/previous actions and by route setupController (admin_group_route.js:13, group-members.js.es6:11), spreading paging logic across model/controller/route with no single owner.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show paging-related state on the Group model (`limit`, `offset`, `user_count`) and controller-level computed properties (`currentPage`, `totalPages`) plus controller actions that mutate `model.offset` and call `model.findMembers()`. Routes also call `model.findMembers()` in `setupController`. However, this is an architectural cohesion concern rather than a concrete defect: there is no verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness failure demonstrated by the diff solely because paging logic is split across model/controller/route. The code still has a clear owner for fetching members (`Group#findMembers`) and the mutations are consistent with Ember patterns (controller actions updating model state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62 — The `// TODO: should clear the input` in `addMembers` is a real gap, not a stale comment: `usernames` is never reset after `model.addMembers()` resolves, so the user-selector input keeps its previous text after a successful add.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action checks `this.get("usernames")` and calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`, but it never clears or resets the controller’s `usernames` property afterward (no `set("usernames", ...)` and no `.then(...)` handler). Since the template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`, leaving `usernames` unchanged will keep the previous text/selection in the input after a successful add. The `// TODO: should clear the input` therefore reflects a real, present UX defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound, so a caller can request e.g. `limit=999999999` on this non-admin, guardian-visible endpoint and force full in-memory materialization and JSON serialization of every member of a large group (old code at least capped automatic groups at 200).

adjudication.rationale: In GroupsController#members the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` and in the JSON response meta, with no maximum enforced. A client who can view the group (via `guardian.ensure_can_see!`) can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing the server to load and serialize a very large member list in one request. However, the finding’s comparison to the old code is partially incorrect: the old code’s `limit` for automatic groups defaulted to 200 but was also not capped (client could still pass a huge limit), and non-automatic groups previously returned all members unbounded. The “no upper bound” issue is still real in the diff, but it’s not newly introduced in the way described.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `members` to always use `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and adds pagination metadata, but the proposed finding hinges on whether there is (or isn’t) an index supporting `users.username_lower` and/or the group membership join. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — addMembers()'s .then callback calls self.findMembers() without returning it, same unreturned/unhandled-rejection issue as removeMember

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, addMembers() returns the promise from Discourse.ajax(...).then(...), but the .then callback just calls self.findMembers() without returning it. That means the promise returned by addMembers() resolves immediately after the PUT succeeds (with undefined), while the follow-up reload request runs “detached”. If findMembers()’s AJAX call fails, its rejection won’t be chained to (or catchable via) the addMembers() promise, and callers cannot reliably wait for the members list to be refreshed. The same pattern exists in removeMember().

Also, “untested” is not inherently a defect introduced by this diff; it’s a process concern unless the diff demonstrably breaks existing tests/behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues xhr :put instead of :delete even though the real route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, so this test never exercises the actual HTTP verb a client would use and only passes because RSpec controller specs invoke the action by name, bypassing route verb matching

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin groups member-removal endpoint is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, while add_members is `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`. In the diff, the spec context ".remove_member" starts with `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, ...`, i.e. it uses PUT to invoke `remove_member`. Rails controller specs will dispatch directly to the action name regardless of routing constraints, so this test would not validate that the DELETE verb/route used by real clients works as intended (and could pass even if the DELETE route were broken).
